_comment: Named, capped, justified exceptions to the 30s release-leaf ceiling in
playmode_gate.py. Every entry needs a fullName, a capSeconds it commits to, and
a reason in prose. An entry without a reason is refused; a leaf that exceeds its
own capSeconds is refused exactly as if it had no entry here. `plan` prints every
applied entry with its reason, and reports entries that have gone stale.
Adding an entry is not a way to make a slow test pass. It is a way to make a
deliberate exception visible in the plan output and in the final report. If the
honest answer is that the test is a soak test, give it [Category("Soak")]
instead -- that moves it to a lane where the ceiling does not apply, which is a

exemptions.reason: 34 real product transitions -- 24 save/loads, 6 restarts, 4 session reopens -- not an endurance ladder. Its unit of work is a whole session rebuild, so it is a genuine short regression that is merely expensive, and Agent 4 examined it and declined to reclassify it as Soak. Trimming the rounds would weaken real coverage to satisfy a number: the test's own documentation relies on the round count for signal-to-noise, since a per-rebuild leak of six objects rather than three thousand still has to clear the noise floor. Measured 54.3s; capped at 75s to leave headroom for machine variance while still refusing if it grows materially.
